title: Choose ShelfLM’s visual world
question: Auth is the first surface. The roll assigned Inkan Seal Desk — a Japanese identity ritual that fits sign-in. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Fixed-width alignment is locked either way.

options.label: Inkan Seal Desk
options.lineage: Japanese hanko / inkan identity ritual on a washi desk
options.thesis: Signing in is pressing your seal: one fixed-width column, vermilion mark, sumi text — identity as a deliberate act, not a SaaS card.
options.viewport: Centered fixed column (~420px): ShelfLM wordmark top, short line, primary seal-action (Google), quiet sign-up/sign-in switch, error as a red seal-stamp note below — everything share one left edge.
options.risk: Seal metaphor can feel ceremonial if the CTA isn’t instantly recognizable as Continue with Google.

raised.raise: Square-centered primary action and one gold/amber active cue — like the fold step marker — so the seal moment feels deliberate, not decorative.
Hairline rule discipline and tabular mono for status/error meta — operate clarity without losing the Japanese desk.
Strict fixed grid cells for the column — every row shares the same measure; no free-floating widths.

options.label: Washi Sumi Stationery
options.lineage: Japanese stationery desk — washi, sumi, vermilion hanko accents
options.thesis: ShelfLM as a writing desk: paper ground, ink hierarchy, fixed margins — learning tools feel like tools you sit down with.
options.viewport: Same fixed column as a letter sheet: brand as letterhead, sign-in as the first written act, Google as the only pen on the desk.
options.risk: Also the direction most Japanese-product runs land on — familiar, effective, less unique than the seal ritual.

options.label: Orizuru Fold Sequence
options.thesis: Auth as fold steps: one square sheet, numbered margin, active crease marked — enter ShelfLM by completing the sequence.
options.viewport: Centered square auth panel; step margin 1·2; primary fold = Continue with Google; failure unfolds one step back.
options.case: Wins audience identification (iconic Japanese craft); loses product clarity for a one-action Google gate.
options.risk: Teaching-fold UI overcomplicates a single OAuth button.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.lineage: Ryoji Ikeda — pure black/white data lattices
options.thesis: Auth as a data gate: monospace, hairline bars, invert on success — Japanese digital austerity at full commitment.
options.viewport: Fixed-width mono column on black; Continue with Google as a selected data row; error as inverted strip.
options.case: Holds product clarity for Operate; loses warm Japanese stationery identification you asked for.
options.risk: Can feel cold/art-installation rather than a learning workspace.

options.label: Doujin Event Catalog
options.lineage: Newsprint circle catalogs at comic markets
options.case: Fuses poorly for auth: packed catalog energy fights a single identity action.
options.kept: Whole-cell fixed grid measure — every block shares one width.

options.label: Cyclorama Dawn
options.lineage: Theater lighting cyclorama — night to day
options.case: Atmospheric theater ≠ Japanese desk tool; weak audience ID for ShelfLM.
options.kept: Named state phases (idle / authenticating / failed) as discrete cues.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.case: Beautiful but not Japanese-pinned; constellation metaphor muddies sign-in.

options.label: Split-Flap Board
options.case: Operate-clear but Western station grammar; fights the Japanese brief.
options.kept: Cascading state change for auth pending → success.

canonCard.label: Category standard auth
canonCard.thesis: Centered card, email/password or social buttons, soft shadow — the SaaS gate executed cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: Logo, headline, Google button, legal line — predictable and clear.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other AI tool login by design.
